 Grand Theft Auto VI's early launch on Xbox Series X may be easier than on PS5. 
 Maxim Boldson 
 GAMES 
 November 02, 2026 
 Views: 1251 
 The gaming community has noted a significant difference in the difficulty of gaining early access to Grand Theft Auto VI between competing current-generation consoles. While PlayStation 5 owners must create a separate regional profile, find foreign top-up cards, and set up shared access to their console to launch the game at midnight in New Zealand, on the Xbox Series platform, this process is completed in a matter of seconds. This is due to fundamental differences in the regional policies of the services: the Microsoft ecosystem does not lock purchased content to the region in which you create your account and allows you to freely switch your operating system's location at any time.
 The technical algorithm for launching a crime action game on Xbox Series consoles consists of five basic steps:
 Turn on your Xbox Series console.
 Open the system settings menu.
 Go to the Settings section, then select System and open the Language and location subsection.
 Change the current system location to New Zealand.
 Restart the console to apply the settings you made.
 The entire region change process takes about 20 seconds and requires no financial costs, no additional gift cards, or multiple accounts. The game remains purchased on the user's primary profile in their home region, but thanks to a temporary region change within the operating system, the unlock timer automatically switches to New Zealand's local time. As a result, American console owners can begin Grand Theft Auto VI 18 hours earlier than the official North American launch, and 10-14 hours earlier than players in most European countries.
